security_audit.summary: All 42 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown links, inline-code formatting, prompt examples, and declarative homepage metadata. The skill is documentation-only and directs writers to treat imported marketing data as untrusted input; no executable command, network request, path traversal, or prompt-injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Static analysis flags Markdown backticks and relative documentation links as command execution and path traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Use scanner rules that distinguish Markdown links and inline-code references from executable shell, Ruby, and filesystem operations.

remediation.issue: The skill names related tools and a registry script without clarifying the execution boundary.
remediation.suggestion: State that any registry proposal is performed only through an approved host integration after user authorization, not by direct shell execution.

content.value_statement: Writing email copy across subject lines, body text, and landing pages can create inconsistent promises. This skill creates a complete email creative with claim flags and a clear message-match check.
actual_capabilities: Drafts three to five labeled subject-line variants for promo, cold-outbound, or newsletter emails.
Creates a matched preheader, structured body copy, one primary call to action, and a plain-text alternative.
Aligns email promises and call-to-action language with a supplied destination page.
Marks unsupported claims with [needs source] instead of inventing evidence.
Applies mode-specific guidance for B2C promotions, B2B cold outreach, and newsletters.
limitations: It does not send emails, manage suppression lists, or access email platforms on its own.
It does not score deliverability, rank subject lines, or calculate email quality scores.
It needs a destination URL to verify message match.
Users remain responsible for legal review, consent, and final approval before sending.

use_cases.title: Launch a promotional email
use_cases.description: Create a promotional email with several subject angles, verified offer wording, and one purchase call to action.

use_cases.title: Prepare a cold outreach message
use_cases.description: Draft a concise B2B email using a genuine personalization signal and a low-pressure reply request.

use_cases.title: Publish a creator newsletter
use_cases.description: Build an editorial newsletter with a clear reader action and an explicitly labeled sponsorship placement.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic promotion
prompt_templates.prompt: Write five subject lines, a preheader, body copy, one CTA, and plain-text email for our summer offer. Destination: https://example.com/summer. Mode: promo.

prompt_templates.title: Create a cold outreach email
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a cold-outbound email for operations leaders at software companies. Offer: workflow audit. Personalization signal: recent hiring. Destination: https://example.com/audit.

prompt_templates.title: Iterate subject-line variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve these losing subject lines while keeping the body and destination promise unchanged: [paste variants]. Destination: [URL]. Mode: newsletter.

prompt_templates.title: Build a claims-aware campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a B2C lifecycle email from these approved claims: [paste claims]. Use this destination: [URL]. Flag unsupported statements with [needs source] and include a message-match map.

output_examples.input: Write a promo email for a 20% discount on annual plans.
output: Subject A: Save 20% on your annual plan
Preheader: Lock in a full year of features before the offer ends.
Body: Explain the approved discount, eligibility, deadline, and one action.
Plain text: A readable version with the same offer and link.

output_examples.input: Draft cold outreach for a workflow audit.
output: Subject A: A faster path through your weekly reporting
Preheader: A short audit can identify manual reporting steps.
Body: Reference the verified signal, explain the audit, and make one low-pressure request.

best_practices: Provide the exact destination URL and approved offer terms before drafting.
Use only verified personalization details and approved claims.
Review consent, disclosures, and final copy before any send.
anti_patterns: Do not promise prices, results, or deadlines without approved evidence.
Do not use fabricated familiarity or misleading urgency in cold outreach.
Do not use multiple competing primary calls to action.

faq.question: Can this skill send an email?
faq.answer: No. It drafts email creative only. Sending requires separate approval and an email platform.

faq.question: How many subject lines does it create?
faq.answer: It normally creates three to five labeled variants with a matched preheader.

faq.question: Can I use it for cold outreach?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports B2B cold outreach with genuine personalization and a low-pressure ask.

faq.question: Does it check legal compliance?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for claims and disclosures, but it does not replace legal or compliance review.

faq.question: Why do I need a destination URL?
faq.answer: The URL lets the skill compare the email promise and CTA with the landing page.

faq.question: What happens when a claim is unsupported?
faq.answer: The skill marks it with [needs source] rather than presenting it as approved.
